type {AddressInfo} from 'node:net';\nimport {WebSocket} from 'ws';\nimport type {Express} from 'express';\nimport {createServer} from './createServer.js';\nimport {HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL} from './ws/subprotocol.js';\nimport {answeringOrchestrator, closeClientsAndStop, delegatingStore} from './wsTestSupport.js';\nimport {InMemorySessionStore} from '../infrastructure/stores/inMemorySessionStore.js';\nimport type {SessionCursor, SessionListOptions, SessionStore, SessionSummary} from '../types/sessionStore.js';\nimport {setLogger} from '../shared/logger.js';\n\n// Real upgrades over a real socket: what the list_sessions frame answers is the contract, and no double can observe it.\n\ninterface Frame {\n  type: string;\n  sessionId?: string;\n  sessions?: Array<{sessionId: string; createdAt: string; updatedAt: string; entryCount: number}>;\n  code?: string;\n  message?: string;\n}\n\nconst servers: Array<ReturnType<typeof createServer>> = [];\nconst clients: WebSocket[] = [];\nconst logLines: Array<{level: string; category: string; message: string; fields?: Record<string, unknown>}> = [];\n\nbeforeEach(() => {\n  logLines.length = 0;\n  const record = (level: string) => (category: string, message: string, fields?: Record<string, unknown>) =>\n    void logLines.push({level, category, message, fields});\n  setLogger({debug: record('debug'), info: record('info'), warn: record('warn'), error: record('error')});\n});\n\nafterEach(async () => {\n  await closeClientsAndStop(clients, servers);\n  setLogger();\n});\n\nconst startEngine = async (store: SessionStore, userId: string | number = 'u1') => {\n  const hal = createServer({\n    app: (() => undefined) as unknown as Express,\n    wsAuth: async () => ({id: userId}),\n    sessionStore: store,\n    orchestrator: answeringOrchestrator,\n  });\n  await hal.start(0);\n  servers.push(hal);\n  const {port} = hal.server.address() as AddressInfo;\n  return `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/hal/ws`;\n};\n\n// The ping sent after the question is the barrier: its pong can only follow every frame the question drew.\nconst sendQuestion = (client: WebSocket, outbound: unknown): void => {\n  client.send(typeof outbound === 'string' ? outbound : JSON.stringify(outbound));\n  client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'ping', timestamp: 1}));\n};\n\nconst askAfterConnect = async (url: string, outbound: unknown): Promise<{connected: Frame; frames: Frame[]}> => {\n  const client = new WebSocket(url, [HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL, 't']);\n  clients.push(client);\n  const frames: Frame[] = [];\n  let connected: Frame = {type: ''};\n  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') {\n        connected = frame;\n        sendQuestion(client, outbound);\n        return;\n      }\n      if (frame.type === 'pong') {\n        resolve();\n        return;\n      }\n      frames.push(frame);\n    });\n  });\n  return {connected, frames};\n};\n\ndescribe('listing conversations over the WebSocket protocol', () => {\n  it('answers list_sessions for the authenticated user with ISO dates, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client userId', async () => {\n    const inner = new InMemorySessionStore();\n    const seen: Array<{userId: string | number; options?: SessionListOptions}> = [];\n    const summaries: SessionSummary[] = [\n      {\n        sessionId: 's2',\n        createdAt: new Date('2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z'),\n        updatedAt: new Date('2026-01-01T00:02:00.000Z'),\n        entryCount: 4,\n      },\n    ];\n    const store: SessionStore = {\n      ...delegatingStore(inner),\n      listFor: (userId, options) => {\n        seen.push({userId, options});\n        return summaries;\n      },\n    };\n    const url = await startEngine(store, 'u1');\n    const before: SessionCursor = {updatedAt: '2026-01-01T00:05:00.000Z', sessionId: 's3'};\n\n    const {frames} = await askAfterConnect(url, {type: 'list_sessions', limit: 10, before, userId: 'u2'});\n\n    expect({seen, frames}).toEqual({\n      seen: [{userId: 'u1', options: {limit: 10, before}}],\n      frames: [\n        {\n          type: 'session_list',\n          sessions: [\n            {\n              sessionId: 's2',\n              createdAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z',\n              updatedAt: '2026-01-01T00:02:00.000Z',\n              entryCount: 4,\n            },\n          ],\n        },\n      ],\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws', async () => {\n    const inner = new InMemorySessionStore();\n    const withoutList = await startEngine(delegatingStore(inner));\n    const failingList = await startEngine({\n      ...delegatingStore(inner),\n      listFor: () => Promise.reject(new Error('database offline')),\n    });\n\n    const unimplemented = await askAfterConnect(withoutList, {type: 'list_sessions'});\n    const failed = await askAfterConnect(failingList, {type: 'list_sessions'});\n\n    expect({\n      unimplemented: unimplemented.frames,\n      failed: failed.frames.map(frame => ({type: frame.type, code: frame.code})),\n      logged: logLines.filter(line => line.level === 'error' && line.category === 'ws'),\n    }).toEqual({\n      unimplemented: [{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}],\n      failed: [{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}],\n      logged: [\n        {\n          level: 'error',\n          category: 'ws',\n          message: expect.any(String),\n          fields: expect.objectContaining({userId: 'u1', error: 'database offline'}),\n        },\n      ],\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('accepts a bare list_sessions frame and rejects a malformed limit or before with INVALID_MESSAGE without calling listFor', async () => {\n    const inner = new InMemorySessionStore();\n    let calls = 0;\n    const store: SessionStore = {\n      ...delegatingStore(inner),\n      listFor: () => {\n        calls += 1;\n        return [];\n      },\n    };\n    const url = await startEngine(store);\n    const badFrames = [\n      {type: 'list_sessions', limit: 'ten'},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', limit: -1},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', limit: 1.5},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', before: 'not-an-object'},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', before: {updatedAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z', sessionId: ''}},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', before: {updatedAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z', sessionId: 'a'.repeat(129)}},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', before: {updatedAt: 'not-a-date', sessionId: 's1'}},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', before: {updatedAt: true, sessionId: 's1'}},\n    ];\n\n    const codes: Array<string | undefined> = [];\n    for (const bad of badFrames) {\n      const {frames} = await askAfterConnect(url, bad);\n      codes.push(frames[0]?.code);\n    }\n    const {frames: accepted} = await askAfterConnect(url, {type: 'list_sessions'});\n\n    expect({codes, accepted, calls}).toEqual({\n      codes: Array(badFrames.length).fill('INVALID_MESSAGE'),\n      accepted: [{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}],\n      calls: 1,\n    });\n  });\n});\n","numLines":186,"startLine":1,"totalLines":186}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_48624425c57f42b3b88050db","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

release = resolve;\n64\t  });\n65\t  return {until, release};\n66\t}\n67\t\n68\t/** Polls `check` every 10 ms for up to half a second, for state a callback wrote on another tick. */\n69\texport async {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_74f506fe03eb41e2a04287e3","type":"tool_result","content":"name: CI\n\non:\n  pull_request:\n  push:\n    branches: [main]\n  # Manual runs: re-checking a branch against a moved main, or confirming a gate after\n  # changing one, without pushing an empty commit.\n  workflow_dispatch:\n  # An advisory published after a merge is invisible until someone opens a pull request, and this\n  # repository can go days without one. Monday 07:00 UTC; only `build-chain` answers it.\n  schedule:\n    - cron: '0 7 * * 1'\n\n# Every job here only reads the checkout; the repo default is write.\npermissions:\n  contents: read\n\n# A newer push to the same branch supersedes an in-flight run. main is exempt:\n# every commit there should have its own recorded result.\nconcurrency:\n  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}\n  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}\n\njobs:\n  verify:\n    name: Verify\n    # The scheduled run exists for the dependency audit; re-running the suite on an unchanged\n    # tree every Monday would report nothing new.\n    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n          # Full history, not for this job but for the spec anchor check below:\n          # it resolves cited content from\n          # origin/main, which a shallow clone cannot serve.\n          fetch-depth: 0\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n        with:\n          node-version: '22'\n          cache: npm\n\n      # --ignore-scripts so `prepare` does not build on install: what a lifecycle script\n      # runs is out of this workflow's control, and the Build step below is where a broken\n      # compile should be reported. Type check catches it earlier still.\n      - name: Install\n        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n\n      # Every `npm run` step below is one link of the `verify` script in\n      # package.json, in the same order - scripts/verify-script.test.ts holds\n      # the two together - and kept as separate steps so a red run names the\n      # gate that failed rather than a single opaque command.\n      - name: Type check\n        run: npm run typecheck\n\n      # example/ is outside tsconfig.json's rootDir, so nothing checked the one\n      # file the README and the guide are written against.\n      - name: Type check the example\n        run: npm run typecheck:example\n\n      - name: Lint (--max-warnings 0)\n        run: npm run eslint\n\n      # Reports, never blocks. The one rule it runs is `warn`, so the step exits\n      # 0 on its own and carries no continue-on-error: a non-zero exit here now\n      # means the config itself broke, and that should fail. Its findings render\n      # as warning annotations rather than failures, which is what a report on a\n      # passing check should look like.\n      #\n      # require-statement-links counts spec statements with no test behind them.\n      # Most of what it reports needs a test written rather than a line changed,\n      # so the count is meant to be visible on every run and to fall over time.\n      # Its test-side mirror, require-spec-link, is satisfied and gates in the\n      # Lint step above. Never add a rule here to escape a red gate -\n      # eslint.config.backlog.mjs says what belongs.\n      - name: Spec traceability backlog (report)\n        run: npm run lint:backlog\n\n      - name: Format check\n        run: npm run prettier:check\n\n      # Runs the whole suite and fails it on the committed coverage floor in\n      # jest.config.js, so this is the test gate rather than an extra pass.\n      - name: Test (with coverage floor)\n        run: npm run test:coverage\n\n      - name: Build\n        run: npm run build\n\n      # Anchors drift silently: a cited file gaining or losing lines above the\n      # cited one leaves the link pointing at different content, and the spec\n      # still reads as cited. Resolves content at origin/main, which the\n      # fetch-depth: 0 above exists to provide. A red check is fixed by running\n      # `node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs` and committing the result.\n      - name: Spec anchor check\n        run: node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs --check origin/main\n\n      # A citation counts as coverage only in its statement's trailing\n      # parenthetical; one written mid-statement is dropped by the Lore job in silence,\n      # so the spec reads as cited while its coverage is zero. A red check is\n      # fixed by moving the link to the end of its statement, never by deleting\n      # it (AGENTS.md § Spec Test Links).\n      # Every fenced typescript block in the three documented files is generated\n      # from source; hand transcription is what produced the defects this catches.\n      - name: Documented code blocks\n        run: npm run docs:check\n\n      # Three rules that held only because somebody remembered them: a path in prose that resolves,\n      # a spike that says it is a spike, and an example region inside the EU.\n      - name: Documented paths resolve\n        run: npm run docs:check-paths\n\n      - name: Spike documents carry a status block\n        run: npm run docs:check-spikes\n\n      - name: Documented regions\n        run: npm run check:regions\n\n      # A line number is a derived pointer; the name is what the author cited. This catches a citation\n      # whose line moved under it, which no baseline comparison can see on a branch that edits the spec.\n      - name: Spec citations name their test\n        run: npm run spec:names\n\n      - name: Spec link placement\n        run: npm run check:spec-links\n\n      # Lead paragraphs and a spec's status-vs-coverage are ESLint's job; the\n      # one verdict a `files` glob cannot express - that an ADR's frontmatter\n      # status parses, without holding the ADR to the coverage tier - is this\n      # script's. `check:spec-status -- --coverage` lists unlinked statements\n      # and never gates.\n      - name: Spec status\n        run: npm run check:spec-status\n\n      # A release note and a commit subject have different readers, so this is a\n      # file the author writes rather than something derived from the log. The\n      # label is the escape hatch for a src/ change nothing installable observes.\n      - name: Changelog entry\n        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'no-changelog')\n        # No fetch: the checkout above resolves every head into refs/remotes\n        # with fetch-depth 0, and its credential is gone by the time a step\n        # runs, so fetching here asked an unauthenticated git for a private\n        # repository and exited 128 before the gate was ever reached.\n        run: bash scripts/check-changelog.sh \"origin/${{ github.base_ref }}\"\n\n  # Separate job, not a step on `verify`: these two check what the build chain\n  # pulls in rather than what the code does, and a red audit should not read as\n  # a failing test suite. It needs the tree installed but nothing built, so it\n  # skips `prepare` with --ignore-scripts.\n  build-chain:\n    name: Build chain\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n        with:\n          node-version: '22'\n          cache: npm\n\n      - name: Install (no build)\n        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n\n      # Full tree, dev included: those packages are what a runner installs\n      # before building dist/, and the release workflow signs what it produces.\n      - name: Audit (high and above)\n        run: npm run check:audit\n\n      # A tag is a mutable pointer its owner can repoint under a job that holds\n      # repository credentials.\n      - name: Action pins\n        run: npm run check:action-pins\n\n  # Its own job because it is the only check that exercises the package as a\n  # consumer receives it - packed, installed outside this tree, with no optional\n  # peer present. Everything else here tests the source in place, where every\n  # dependency is already installed and every one of these failures is invisible.\n  smoke:\n    name: Smoke (packed tarball)\n    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n        with:\n          node-version: '22'\n          cache: npm\n\n      - name: Install (no build)\n        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n\n      # Explicit, rather than relying on `npm pack` to trigger `prepare`: a build failure should be\n      # reported by a step named Build, not as a confusing pack error inside the smoke script.\n      - name: Build\n        run: npm run build\n\n      # Two variants, two jobs' worth of signal in one: `bare` is a mock-provider consumer with no\n      # optional peer, `full` is a Bedrock or Vertex consumer with both. They fail differently and\n      # separate steps name which consumer is broken.\n      - name: Smoke (no optional peer)\n        run: npm run smoke -- bare\n\n      - name: Smoke (both optional peers)\n        run: npm run smoke -- full","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"6a3e212e-6e3b-4d2a-9c54-071d7692face","uuid":"ddd5c315-ff6a-4e0a-91c7-3a7887e91b81","timestamp":"2026-11-03T14:10:48.631Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"name: CI\n\non:\n  pull_request:\n  push:\n    branches: [main]\n  # Manual runs: re-checking a branch against a moved main, or confirming a gate after\n  # changing one, without pushing an empty commit.\n  workflow_dispatch:\n  # An advisory published after a merge is invisible until someone opens a pull request, and this\n  # repository can go days without one. error.message : String(error);\n    return {ok: false, reason: reason.split('\\n')[0]};\n  }\n}\n\nconst consoleLogger: Logger = {\n  debug: (category: string, message: string, fields?: Record<string, unknown>) =>\n    emit('DEBUG', category, message, fields),\n  info: (category: string, message: string, fields?: Record<string, unknown>) =>\n    emit('INFO', category, message, fields),\n  warn: (category: string, message: string, fields?: Record<string, unknown>) =>\n    emit('WARN', category, message, fields),\n  error: (category: string, message: string, fields?: Record<string, unknown>) =>\n    emit('ERROR', category, message, fields),\n};\n\nlet active: Logger = consoleLogger;\n\n// Process-global by design: every module that logs imports `log` at module scope, so there is one.\nexport function setLogger(logger?: Logger): void {\n  // Handed `log` itself, the delegate below would call itself until the stack ran out, so that reads as none.\n  active = logger === undefined || logger === log ? {"type":"assistant","message":{"id":"msg_202611032214054a590def3ba64f70","type":"message","role":"assistant","model":"glm-5.3-flash","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"VERY interesting! Two findings:\n\n1. `frames after ask 2 (no listFor): []` — the store WITHOUT `listFor` returned NO frames at all! The acceptance test expects `[{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}]`. Wait — in my probe, ask 2 got ZERO frames. Hmm, but the pong arrived (the promise resolved), yet no session_list frame arrived?? Wait — the frames array only collects non-connected non-pong frames. The pong resolved the promise — but the session_list should have arrived BEFORE or AFTER the pong...\n\nOH WAIT. I see — there's a RACE. The server sends `connected`, then the client sends list_sessions + ping back-to-back. The server's message handler processes list_sessions ASYNC (`answerListSessions` awaits `sessionStore?.listFor?.(...)` — even for the no-listFor store, `sessionStore?.listFor?.()` returns undefined immediately, but the function is ASYNC so `sendSessionList` happens on a microtask AFTER the ping's pong?). Neither hangs by itself...\n\n`lore-list-tests.mjs` runs `npx jest --json` over the WHOLE SUITE. If ONE test hangs forever, this hangs forever → 15-min timeout. And with `--json` output to a file and stdout/stderr ignored/inherit, we'd see jest's progress on stderr — the brief's captured output could be exactly that.\n\nSo the hang is ONE test that never completes. Jest's per-test timeout SHOULD bound it... Let me reconsider jest's testTimeout semantics once more. `test(fn, timeout)` — the timeout applies when the test function returns a promise: jest fails the test if the promise doesn't settle within the timeout. TRUE for `it('...', async () => {...})`. So a hanging await fails at 5s.\n\nHmm, but WAIT — what does jest do when a test TIMES OUT but the underlying promise LATER resolves? {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_f23f0ee8fde24fa79c078b49","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t---\n2\tadr_number: 6\n3\ttitle: Four re-lint rules suppressed where they misread the domain\n4\tstatus: accepted\n5\tdate: 2026-09-10\n6\tdomains:\n7\t  - tooling\n8\t  - lint\n9\t  - ai-providers\n10\t  - transport\n11\t---\n12\t\n13\t# ADR-006: Four re-lint rules suppressed where they misread the domain\n14\t\n15\tThis ADR records four inline suppressions of `@re-cinq/eslint-plugin-re-lint` rules, and why each is a mismatch between a good rule and this repo's domain rather than debt to be paid down. Every other finding the rules report stays reported: three of the four rules remain enabled and still fire elsewhere in the tree, and the suppressions are per-site with a reason attached, never a rule switched off repo-wide. The alternative in each case was to change working code in a direction that made it worse - a breaking public API change, an eagerly-loaded SDK, a lost type narrowing at a trust boundary, and a deleted regression pin. This decision is implemented.\n16\t\n17\t## Context\n18\t\n19\t`eslint.config.mjs` enables 31 of re-lint's 39 rules, several of which other adopters decline. Enabling them was deliberate: the instruction was to integrate every applicable linter and let it fail rather than refactor to suit it, so the backlog would be visible. Working through that backlog separates cleanly into findings whose fix improves the code and findings whose fix does not. These four are the second kind. They were identified while clearing the mechanical findings, each verified by reading the rule's own source or probing it, not inferred from the message text.\n20\t\n21\t## Decision\n22\t\n23\tFive sites carry `eslint-disable-next-line` (or, in one case, a file-level `eslint-disable`) with a `--` reason referring here, under the four decisions below. Together they account for every finding these three rules report: run with `--no-inline-config` and the count is three `no-flag-params`, one `prefer-polymorphism` and one `test-imports-its-subject`. The sixth was withdrawn when its rule stopped firing - see the `validateMessage` entry.\n24\t\n25\t**`re-lint/no-flag-params` on `AIError`'s `retryable` parameter** (`src/types/ai.ts`). `AIError` is exported from `src/index.ts` and `retryable` is a `public readonly` constructor parameter, so it is part of the published API. The rule's remedy - split the function into two named functions - means two error classes or two factories, which is a breaking change for every consumer constructing an `AIError`. CLAUDE.md routes breaking changes through an issue, a migration guide, a MINOR bump and a deprecation period; a lint sweep is not that process.\n26\t\n27\tThe same constraint reaches every other site that constructs a retryable `AIError`, because `retryable` defaults to `false` and there is no other way to express one. Two carry the same suppression: `mapVertexError` in `src/providers/vertex/vertexProvider.ts`, which classifies a rate limit, and one call site in `src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts`, which builds the error a handler is expected to surface. In both the rule's premise is false in the same way - the boolean is not selecting a behaviour, it is a field of a value.\n28\t\n29\tTwo further sites in `src/providers/vertex/vertexProvider.test.ts` carried this suppression until those tests stopped constructing an expected `AIError` at all. Asserting on the thrown error's `name`, `code` and `retryable` fields is both stricter and free of the literal: `expect(...).rejects.toThrow(new AIError(msg, code, true))` compares only the message, so it passed against a deliberately mis-classified error.\n30\t\n31\t**`re-lint/prefer-polymorphism` on `createProvider`** (`src/providers/providerFactory.ts`). The five-way `switch` on `config.type` narrows a discriminated union onto five factories that take five different config types. A lookup table keyed by the string loses that narrowing: TypeScript cannot prove the selected arm's parameter matches the value being dispatched, so the table needs a cast at exactly the point the union was buying safety. This is the same premise as the `validateMessage` entry below, and it is not the premise this entry carried before the ESM conversion. Until then each arm `require`d its provider's module lazily and the suppression was justified as a loading boundary - but `src/index.ts` statically re-exports all five factories, so the factory's laziness never prevented a single module load. The boundary that does work lives inside each provider, around the vendor SDK, and stays there.\n32\t\n33\t**`re-lint/prefer-polymorphism` on `validateMessage`** (`src/transport/ws/validation.ts`). Withdrawn, not reversed. The `switch` on `message.type` narrows an untrusted WebSocket frame through a discriminated union, and a lookup keyed by string would lose that narrowing at precisely the point where the input is attacker-controlled and the type is a claim rather than a fact. The `default` arm rejecting unknown types is the security behaviour. But removing the `send_message` alias left the switch with two cases, below the rule's threshold, so the rule no longer fires and the directive became an unused-disable error. It is deleted. The reasoning above stands and the suppression should come back with it the moment a third case is added - which the add-a-message-type how-to walks a reader straight into.\n34\t\n35\t**`re-lint/test-imports-its-subject` on the layering test** (`scripts/eslint-layers.test.ts`). The rule reports that the file loads no first-party module and so cannot fail when production code changes. It does exercise the real `eslint.config.mjs` - through `spawnSync`, because loading a flat config in-process needs `--experimental-vm-modules` - and the rule cannot see through a subprocess. The file exists because the layering gate's failure mode is silence: `no-cross-layer-import` keys packages by `<package>/src/`, so a misconfigured root matches nothing, reports nothing and looks adopted, which is exactly the state this repo was in until it was probed. Deleting or rewriting the test to satisfy the rule removes the only thing that would notice.\n36\t\n37\t## Rationale\n38\t\n39\tA suppression is honest when the rule's premise is false for the site, and dishonest when it is merely inconvenient. Each of these four fails the rule's premise: the \"function\" is a public constructor, the \"dispatch\" is a loading boundary, the \"dispatch\" is a type narrowing, and the \"test that loads nothing real\" loads the config under test in another process. In each case the rule's suggested remedy is a change that a reviewer would reject on its merits.\n40\t\n41\tPer-site suppression with a written reason was preferred over disabling any rule repo-wide, because three of the four rules have genuine findings elsewhere that should keep failing. `no-flag-params` reports four other sites, `prefer-polymorphism` one, and both counts should fall.\n42\t\n43\t## Consequences\n44\t\n45\t- Five findings no longer appear across the four decisions; two of the three rules keep firing elsewhere.\n46\t- A future reader who removes a suppression sees the reason in the `--` clause before deciding.\n47\t- The suppressions are load-bearing in one direction: if `AIError` is ever redesigned through the breaking-change process, or the provider factory becomes async, the corresponding suppression should be reconsidered rather than carried forward.\n48\t- `re-lint/no-forwarding-class` remains enabled and inert for an unrelated reason - it needs type information this config does not provide - and is documented at its site in `eslint.config.mjs`, not here.\n49\t\n50\t## Alternatives considered\n51\t\n52\t**Refactor to satisfy each rule.** Rejected: a breaking API change outside the documented process, an eager-loading regression, a lost narrowing at a trust boundary, and a deleted anti-silence pin.\n53\t\n54\t**Disable the three rules repo-wide.** Rejected: the suppressions are per-site and visible, and each names its reason. Turning the rules off would silence them for code not yet written, which is where their value is.\n55\t\n56\t**Leave all four failing.** Rejected: a gate that reports findings nobody intends to act on trains readers to ignore it, and these four would never be acted on.\n57\t\n58\t## References\n59\t\n60\t- `eslint.config.mjs` — the enabled rule set and the `no-forwarding-class` inertness note\n61\t- `eslint.config.backlog.mjs` — `require-statement-links` at `warn`, held out of the blocking gate because `npm run eslint` runs `--max-warnings 0`\n62\t- [layers.yaml](../layers.yaml) — the layering the suppressed test pins\n63\t- [src/types/ai.ts](../src/types/ai.ts), [src/providers/providerFactory.ts](../src/providers/providerFactory.ts), [src/transport/ws/validation.ts](../src/transport/ws/validation.ts), [scripts/eslint-layers.test.ts](../scripts/eslint-layers.test.ts)\n64\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"6a3e212e-6e3b-4d2a-9c54-071d7692face","uuid":"dfb85495-8bc4-43f2-9c8c-cc080c755a9e","timestamp":"2026-11-03T14:21:00.750Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/1b5fccac6c68/workspace/target/adrs/ADR-006-lint-suppressions.md","content":"---\nadr_number: 6\ntitle: Four re-lint rules suppressed where they misread the domain\nstatus: accepted\ndate: 2026-09-10\ndomains:\n  - tooling\n  - lint\n  - ai-providers\n  - transport\n---\n\n# ADR-006: Four re-lint rules suppressed where they misread the domain\n\nThis ADR records four inline suppressions of `@re-cinq/eslint-plugin-re-lint` rules, and why each is a mismatch between a good rule and this repo's domain rather than debt to be paid down. Every other finding the rules report stays reported: three of the four rules remain enabled and still fire elsewhere in the tree, and the suppressions are per-site with a reason attached, never a rule switched off repo-wide. The alternative in each case was to change working code in a direction that made it worse - a breaking public API change, an eagerly-loaded SDK, a lost type narrowing at a trust boundary, and a deleted regression pin. This decision is implemented.\n\n## Context\n\n`eslint.config.mjs` enables 31 of re-lint's 39 rules, several of which other adopters decline. Enabling them was deliberate: the instruction was to integrate every applicable linter and let it fail rather than refactor to suit it, so the backlog would be visible. Working through that backlog separates cleanly into findings whose fix improves the code and findings whose fix does not. These four are the second kind. They were identified while clearing the mechanical findings, each verified by reading the rule's own source or probing it, not inferred from the message text.\n\n## Decision\n\nFive sites carry `eslint-disable-next-line` (or, in one case, a file-level `eslint-disable`) with a `--` reason referring here, under the four decisions below. Together they account for every finding these three rules report: run with `--no-inline-config` and the count is three `no-flag-params`, one `prefer-polymorphism` and one `test-imports-its-subject`. The sixth was withdrawn when its rule stopped firing - see the `validateMessage` entry.\n\n**`re-lint/no-flag-params` on `AIError`'s `retryable` parameter** (`src/types/ai.ts`). `AIError` is exported from `src/index.ts` and `retryable` is a `public readonly` constructor parameter, so it is part of the published API. The rule's remedy - split the function into two named functions - means two error classes or two factories, which is a breaking change for every consumer constructing an `AIError`. CLAUDE.md routes breaking changes through an issue, a migration guide, a MINOR bump and a deprecation period; a lint sweep is not that process.\n\nThe same constraint reaches every other site that constructs a retryable `AIError`, because `retryable` defaults to `false` and there is no other way to express one. Two carry the same suppression: `mapVertexError` in `src/providers/vertex/vertexProvider.ts`, which classifies a rate limit, and one call site in `src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts`, which builds the error a handler is expected to surface. In both the rule's premise is false in the same way - the boolean is not selecting a behaviour, it is a field of a value.\n\nTwo further sites in `src/providers/vertex/vertexProvider.test.ts` carried this suppression until those tests stopped constructing an expected `AIError` at all. Asserting on the thrown error's `name`, `code` and `retryable` fields is both stricter and free of the literal: `expect(...).rejects.toThrow(new AIError(msg, code, true))` compares only the message, so it passed against a deliberately mis-classified error.\n\n**`re-lint/prefer-polymorphism` on `createProvider`** (`src/providers/providerFactory.ts`). The five-way `switch` on `config.type` narrows a discriminated union onto five factories that take five different config types. A lookup table keyed by the string loses that narrowing: TypeScript cannot prove the selected arm's parameter matches the value being dispatched, so the table needs a cast at exactly the point the union was buying safety. This is the same premise as the `validateMessage` entry below, and it is not the premise this entry carried before the ESM conversion. Until then each arm `require`d its provider's module lazily and the suppression was justified as a loading boundary - but `src/index.ts` statically re-exports all five factories, so the factory's laziness never prevented a single module load. The boundary that does work lives inside each provider, around the vendor SDK, and stays there.\n\n**`re-lint/prefer-polymorphism` on `validateMessage`** (`src/transport/ws/validation.ts`). Withdrawn, not reversed. The `switch` on `message.type` narrows an untrusted WebSocket frame through a discriminated union, and a lookup keyed by string would lose that narrowing at precisely the point where the input is attacker-controlled and the type is a claim rather than a fact. The `default` arm rejecting unknown types is the security behaviour. But removing the `send_message` alias left the switch with two cases, below the rule's threshold, so the rule no longer fires and the directive became an unused-disable error. It is deleted. The reasoning above stands and the suppression should come back with it the moment a third case is added - which the add-a-message-type how-to walks a reader straight into.\n\n**`re-lint/test-imports-its-subject` on the layering test** (`scripts/eslint-layers.test.ts`). The rule reports that the file loads no first-party module and so cannot fail when production code changes. It does exercise the real `eslint.config.mjs` - through `spawnSync`, because loading a flat config in-process needs `--experimental-vm-modules` - and the rule cannot see through a subprocess. The file exists because the layering gate's failure mode is silence: `no-cross-layer-import` keys packages by `<package>/src/`, so a misconfigured root matches nothing, reports nothing and looks adopted, which is exactly the state this repo was in until it was probed. Deleting or rewriting the test to satisfy the rule removes the only thing that would notice.\n\n## Rationale\n\nA suppression is honest when the rule's premise is false for the site, and dishonest when it is merely inconvenient. Each of these four fails the rule's premise: the \"function\" is a public constructor, the \"dispatch\" is a loading boundary, the \"dispatch\" is a type narrowing, and the \"test that loads nothing real\" loads the config under test in another process. In each case the rule's suggested remedy is a change that a reviewer would reject on its merits.\n\nPer-site suppression with a written reason was preferred over disabling any rule repo-wide, because three of the four rules have genuine findings elsewhere that should keep failing. `no-flag-params` reports four other sites, `prefer-polymorphism` one, and both counts should fall.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Five findings no longer appear across the four decisions; two of the three rules keep firing elsewhere.\n- A future reader who removes a suppression sees the reason in the `--` clause before deciding.\n- The suppressions are load-bearing in one direction: if `AIError` is ever redesigned through the breaking-change process, or the provider factory becomes async, the corresponding suppression should be reconsidered rather than carried forward.\n- `re-lint/no-forwarding-class` remains enabled and inert for an unrelated reason - it needs type information this config does not provide - and is documented at its site in `eslint.config.mjs`, not here.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n**Refactor to satisfy each rule.** Rejected: a breaking API change outside the documented process, an eager-loading regression, a lost narrowing at a trust boundary, and a deleted anti-silence pin.\n\n**Disable the three rules repo-wide.** Rejected: the suppressions are per-site and visible, and each names its reason. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_c49c873e1aa14176b4897ad9","type":"tool_result","content":"66:## Spec Header Table\n128:## Spec Test Links\n---\n## Spec Test Links\n\nStatements in `specs/*/spec.md` cite their validating test in a trailing\nparenthetical at the end of the statement, where a list item counts as one\nstatement and a paragraph counts per sentence. Tests live beside their source\nin this repo, so the path points into `src/`:\n\n```markdown\n- All entries within a single assistant response are committed before the next\n  user message is processed\n  ([validated by: commits every entry before the next user message](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L42)).\n```\n\nThe citation carries the test's **name** as well as its line. The name is what the\nauthor cited; the line is a derived pointer, and it goes stale on its own - adding\nan import above a suite moves every test below it, and the citation lands on a\ndifferent, still-valid declaration without anything noticing. `npm run spec:names`\nholds each citation to the test it names, and `npm run spec:names:fix` repoints the\nline from the name. The `#Lnn` stays because the lint rule and the coverage job\nboth index by it; a citation without one marks the whole file covered rather than\none test.\n\nA citation counts as coverage only where it is trailing, and a test link placed\nanywhere else in the statement is a misplaced citation rather than a weaker one.\nUpstream `check:spec-links` reports it and exits 1, and the coverage job that\nconsumes these specs records nothing for it - so a spec can read as fully cited while its coverage is\nzero. A mid-statement link to something that is not a test file - a script, a\ndoc, another spec - is ordinary prose, is never reported, and was never coverage\nto begin with. A misplaced citation is fixed by moving it to the end of its\nstatement, never by deleting it.\n\nIn a test file the `#Lnn` anchor must land on the `it(`, `test(` or `describe(`\ndeclaration itself - not a blank line, not one holding only closing punctuation,\nand not a line inside the test body. A citation onto an `expect` renders and\nresolves like any other, and proves nothing: no reader can turn that line back\ninto the name of a case. `scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs` reports all four as\n`rotten` and exits 1 in both modes. A citation into a file that is not a test -\na workflow, a config, `package.json` - has no declaration to land on and is held\nonly to existing and carrying content.\n\nWhat no gate can catch is an anchor aimed at the wrong declaration: a real but\nunintended `it(` passes every check. The tell is that the test the statement\nmeant to cite goes on reading as uncited in the `require-spec-link` backlog.\n\nAnchors drift silently whenever a cited file gains or loses lines above them, so\nafter editing any cited file re-run `node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs`\nrather than hand-correcting the numbers. That script cannot repair a spec absent\nfrom the base ref, since it has no baseline to translate from; on the branch that\nintroduces a spec, its anchors have to be corrected by hand.\n\nThe convention's tooling is wired up here: `npm run check:spec-links`, `npm run check:spec-status` and\n`node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs --check origin/main` all gate CI, and\n`re-lint/require-status-matches-coverage` derives each `Status` row from its\nspec's citations. `re-lint/require-spec-link` gates in `eslint.config.mjs`: every test cites a\nstatement, so an uncited new test fails the build. Its statement-side mirror,\n`require-statement-links`, runs at `warn` from `eslint.config.backlog.mjs` and\nreports without blocking - the severities the rule pair is designed for.\n\n## Commit Conventions","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"6a3e212e-6e3b-4d2a-9c54-071d7692face","uuid":"c048b9b4-d82b-42ed-bbc2-5e50c8c3f019","timestamp":"2026-11-03T14:22:09.906Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"66:## Spec Header Table\n128:## Spec Test Links\n---\n## Spec Test Links\n\nStatements in `specs/*/spec.md` cite their validating test in a trailing\nparenthetical at the end of the statement, where a list item counts as one\nstatement and a paragraph counts per sentence. Unparseable JSON is the one frame answered with `INVALID_FORMAT` and no `stream_end`, because the server cannot tell what it was meant to be; for it the client falls back on the socket closing.\n\n### 5.9 session_list\n\nAnswers a `list_sessions` frame (Section 4.3). It carries no conversation content and no credentials, so a history list cannot leak an entry ([validated by: answers list_sessions for the authenticated user with ISO dates, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client userId](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L80)).\n\nSemantics:\n\n- The list is the authenticated connection's own. The handler reads the user from the session the connection opened and hands the frame's `limit` and `before` to the store, so a `userId` on the frame names nobody ([validated by: answers from the session's own user, forwarding the frame's limit and before, with ISO date strings](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L874)).\n- A store that implements no `listFor` answers an empty `session_list` ([validated by: answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L121), [validated by: answers a store without listFor with an empty list, and a failing one with an error that names no store detail](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L916)).\n- A `listFor` that fails answers one `error` frame with code `SERVER_ERROR` whose message names no store detail, and the failure is logged on the `ws` category ([validated by: answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L121)).\n\n## 6. SessionEntry Objects\n\nA SessionEntry represents a single piece of content in the conversation. Every entry has a `role` field that determines its shape. The handler reads the user from the session the connection opened and hands the frame's `limit` and `before` to the store, so a `userId` on the frame names nobody ([validated by: answers from the session's own user, forwarding the frame's limit and before, with ISO date strings](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L874)).\n- A store that implements no `listFor` answers an empty `session_list` ([validated by: answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L121), [validated by: answers a store without listFor with an empty list, and a failing one with an error that names no store detail](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L916)).\n- A `listFor` that fails answers one `error` frame with code `SERVER_ERROR` whose message names no store detail, and the failure is logged on the `ws` category ([validated by: answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L121)).\n\n## 6. SessionEntry Objects\n\nA SessionEntry represents a single piece of content in the conversation. Every entry has a `role` field that determines its shape. The `role` acts as a discriminant for the union type.","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_4539d19df74e473bb74b460c","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

TOOL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED} from '../../orchestration/chatOrchestrator.js';\nimport type {ChatOrchestrator} from '../../orchestration/chatOrchestrator.js';\nimport {ToolRegistry} from '../../orchestration/tools/registry.js';\nimport {PromptBuilder} from '../../infrastructure/builders/promptBuilder.js';\nimport type {AIProvider, MessageChunk, ToolCall} from '../../types/ai.js';\nimport {AIError} from '../../types/ai.js';\nimport type {ChatSession, SessionEntry} from '../../types/session.js';\nimport type {SessionListOptions, SessionStore} from '../../types/sessionStore.js';\nimport type {OutgoingMessage} from '../../types/messages.js';\nimport {PerSessionLock} from '../../shared/perSessionLock.js';\nimport {deferred} from '../wsTestSupport.js';\n\n// The frames, in order, are the contract - above all for suppression, which retracts.\n\n// One line per frame; entries carry generated timestamps no assertion should read.\nconst wire = (sent: OutgoingMessage[]): string[] =>\n  sent.map(frame => {\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_upsert') {\n      const content = 'content' in frame.entry ? frame.entry.content : '';\n      return `upsert ${frame.index} ${frame.entry.role} ${JSON.stringify(content)}`;\n    }\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_delta') return `delta ${frame.index} ${JSON.stringify(frame.delta)}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_commit') return `commit ${frame.index}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_skip') return `skip ${frame.index}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'error') return `error ${frame.code}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'pong') return `pong ${frame.timestamp}`;\n    return frame.type;\n  });\n\nconst text = (value: string): MessageChunk => ({type: 'text', text: value});\nconst STOP: MessageChunk = {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn'};\nconst SUPPRESS = {type: 'suppress_output'} as unknown as MessageChunk;\n\ninterface StreamScript {\n  failWith?: Error;\n  pauseAfter?: {chunks: number; until: Promise<void>};\n}\n\nconst harness = (chunks: MessageChunk[], {failWith, pauseAfter}: StreamScript = {}) => {\n  const sent: OutgoingMessage[] = [];\n  const ws = {send: (raw: string) => sent.push(JSON.parse(raw) as OutgoingMessage)} as unknown as WebSocket;\n\n  const stream = async function* (): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n    for (const [position, chunk] of chunks.entries()) {\n      if (pauseAfter && position === pauseAfter.chunks) await pauseAfter.until;\n      yield chunk;\n    }\n    if (failWith) throw failWith;\n  };\n\n  const processMessageStream = jest.fn(stream);\n  const orchestrator = {processMessageStream} as unknown as ChatOrchestrator;\n  const session: ChatSession = {sessionId: 's1', userId: 'u1', entries: []};\n\n  const handle = createMessageHandler(orchestrator);\n\n  return {\n    session,\n    processMessageStream,\n    sent,\n    frames: () => wire(sent),\n    send: (raw: unknown = {type: 'user_message', content: 'hello'}, signal?: AbortSignal) =>\n      handle(ws, session, raw, signal),\n  };\n};\n\ndescribe('the websocket message handler', () => {\n  describe('dispatch', () => {\n    it('rejects an unparseable message and never starts a stream', async () => {\n      const h = harness([]);\n\n      await h.send({type: 'nonsense'});\n\n      const {calls} = h.processMessageStream.mock;\n\n      expect({frames: h.frames(), streams: calls.length}).toEqual({frames: ['error INVALID_MESSAGE'], streams: 0});\n    });\n\n    it('answers a ping with the timestamp it was given', async () => {\n      const h = harness([]);\n\n      await h.send({type: 'ping', timestamp: 1234});\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual(['pong 1234']);\n    });\n  });\n\n  describe('a plain assistant reply', () => {\n    it('sends the user entry, then the assistant entry, its delta, its commit and stream_end', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('hi there'), STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual([\n        'upsert 0 user \"hello\"',\n        'upsert 1 assistant \"\"',\n        'delta 1 \"hi there\"',\n        'commit 1',\n        'stream_end',\n      ]);\n    });\n\n    it('leaves the committed assistant entry in the session, no longer streaming', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('hi there'), STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      const {entries} = h.session;\n\n      expect(entries[1]).toMatchObject({role: 'assistant', content: 'hi there', isStreaming: false});\n    });\n  });\n\n  describe('thinking segments', () => {\n    it('commits the thinking entry before the assistant entry opens', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('<thinking>pondering</thinking>answer'), STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual([\n        'upsert 0 user \"hello\"',\n        'upsert 1 thinking \"\"',\n        'delta 1 \"pondering\"',\n        'commit 1',\n        'upsert 2 assistant \"\"',\n        'delta 2 \"answer\"',\n        'commit 2',\n        'stream_end',\n      ]);\n    });\n\n    it('commits the thinking entry when text resumes, not when a tool entry appears', async () => {\n      const h = harness([\n        text('<thinking>I should look up the weather for Berlin.</thinking>'),\n        {type: 'tool_use', toolCall: {id: 'c1', name: 'get_weather', input: {location: 'Berlin'}}} as MessageChunk,\n        text('Berlin currently has '),\n        text('a temperature of 18 degrees Celsius with clear skies.'),\n        STOP,\n      ]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual([\n        'upsert 0 user \"hello\"',\n        'upsert 1 thinking \"\"',\n        'delta 1 \"I should look up the weather for Berlin.\"',\n        'upsert 2 tool \"\"',\n        'commit 1',\n        'upsert 3 assistant \"\"',\n        'delta 3 \"Berlin currently has \"',\n        'delta 3 \"a temperature of 18 degrees Celsius with clear skies.\"',\n        'commit 3',\n        'stream_end',\n      ]);\n    });\n  });\n\n  describe('tool chunks', () => {\n    it('sends a tool entry for a tool call', async () => {\n      const h = harness([{type: 'tool_use', toolCall: return 0;\n  }\n\n  log.debug('stream', 'chunk', {type: chunk.type});\n  return 0;\n}\n\nfunction processChunk(\n  ws: WebSocket,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  state: StreamState,\n  parser: processSuppressChunk(ws, session, state);\n  if (chunk.type === 'stop') return processStopChunk(ws, session, state, parser);\n}\n\nfunction processTextChunk(\n  ws: WebSocket,\n  session:
